body:
Comment write-path test: record and independent receipt. Owner decision: **narrow automated-comment exception approved**; this is its first permitted use.

**Test.** Six comments on this Issue, each from a known source file:

| Comment | Path | Comment id | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| CA | MCP `add_issue_comment` | 7079022382 | plain Markdown: table, code spans, bold, Issue and comment links, SHA in code |
| CB | MCP `add_issue_comment` | 7079022598 | one blob link |
| CC | MCP `add_issue_comment` | 7079022834 | ends with the footer |
| CA-gh | `gh api -X POST …/comments -F body=@file` | 7079028678 | as CA |
| CB-gh | `gh api` | 7079028895 | as CB |
| CC-gh | `gh api` | 7079029073 | as CC |

**Results, confirmed by an independent reviewer session by exact string comparison of fetched bodies against the decoded sources:**

- Neither path stores a comment byte-exact.
- Footer normalization is deterministic and identical on both paths: `stored == core(source) + "\n\n\n---\n" + F`. Here F is the standard footer line. `core()` removes trailing newlines, then one trailing separator-and-footer block if present, then trailing newlines again. Everything before the footer is preserved byte for byte. This was observed for CA, CC, CA-gh and CC-gh.
- Blob links are wrapped in backticks on both paths, so CB and CB-gh fail the rule; reversing only that wrap restores it.
- No other byte differences: no CR, no escaping change, no edit after posting. This Issue was the only target.

**Exception, as approved.**

- Paths: MCP `add_issue_comment` and `gh api -X POST …/comments -F body=@file`. Comments only.
- Blob links are rejected before submission.
- Each comment needs a known local source and SHA-256.
- Every posted comment is fetched and compared byte for byte with the expected normalized text. Any mismatch halts that path, and both versions are preserved.
- Initially only the tested Markdown patterns are used. Others need controlled validation first.
- Issue bodies, PR descriptions and every other automated write remain under the §A.26 halt.

body:
Independent review of the #1548 comment write-path test: all three claims CONFIRMED. The narrow exception HOLDS, with conditions.

Method (read-only; nothing posted, edited or pushed): I fetched each comment with `gh api repos/amaybaum/incompleteness/issues/comments/<id>`, decoded each base64 source myself, and compared them with Python exact string equality.

Source sha256 (decoded) / stored-body sha256:
- CA 7079022382: src 56abeba0…3393 / stored 9edb51c5…74ba
- CB 7079022598: src 449cfb00…db13 / stored f0e578d9…d332
- CC 7079022834: src f9b2cdb7…061f / stored 1054242e…6bc6
- CA-gh 7079028678: src 52c703ea…f557 / stored 541f6a99…23e8
- CB-gh 7079028895: src 1f6bfcb5…016b / stored c6b07964…ee1e
- CC-gh 7079029073: src 652b7e9c…d2e8 / stored 92d06921…c449

Claim 1, no path stores a comment byte-exact: CONFIRMED. stored == source is False for all six.

Claim 2, footer normalization: CONFIRMED. stored == core(source) + "\n\n\n---\n" + F is True for CA, CC, CA-gh and CC-gh. The text before the footer is preserved byte for byte, and the two paths behave the same. For CC and CC-gh, a source footer separated by one blank line ("\n\n---\n"+F+"\n") is rewritten with two blank lines and no trailing newline, as the rule predicts.

Claim 3, blob links: CONFIRMED. On both paths the link becomes "[guide](` https://github.com/amaybaum/incompleteness/blob/8dd58694…/README.md `)", so CB and CB-gh fail the rule. When I reverse only that wrap, stored == core(source)+"\n\n\n---\n"+F is True for both. The wrap is therefore the only extra change, and it stops the link from working.

Other byte differences: none. There is no CR, no trailing newline after the footer, and no other whitespace or escaping change. The table, code spans, bold text, Issue and comment links and the SHA in code all survive exactly. created_at == updated_at on all six, so none were edited after posting. All six show user amaybaum, posted via the app "claude".

Scope: #1548 is open, titled "WRITE-PATH-TEST (disposable; not research)", and has exactly 6 comments: these six. I listed repo-wide Issue comments since 2026-11-22T12:00Z. Besides these six, there are only five comments on #1169 from 12:01–12:09Z (7078817219, 7078832152, 7078857457, 7078898430, 7078919439), all posted before the test window (12:18:49–12:19:24Z). 7078919439 is the comment CA links to. No PR review comments were found in the window. #1548 is the only Issue the test wrote to.

Verdict: the narrow exception HOLDS. It holds for automated comments that contain no blob links, on either path (MCP add_issue_comment or gh api -F body=@file), provided each one is checked after posting by exact comparison of the fetched body with core(source) + "\n\n\n---\n" + F. Any mismatch should be treated as a failure. Limits: the evidence covers 4 passing comments of the content types listed above; other constructs are unverified until they pass the same post-check. A body with a blob link cannot meet the rule on either path.

Owner decision recorded: #1548 designated as the reusable write-path test Issue; one REST Issue-body validation write granted.

Owner decision (amaybaum, 2026-11-25, coordinating session), quoted:

"Use #1548 as the designated scratch Issue, since it was created specifically for write-path testing.

* Commit and push the write-safety protocol, controls and failure evidence to the dedicated evidence branch.

* Preserve #1548's existing body byte for byte, including its original evidence and hashes, before performing the validation write.

* Perform one controlled REST Issue-body validation write on #1548. Establish the exact expected stored text before writing, including any documented attribution footer.

* Verify the complete stored body byte for byte. If it differs, stop the affected mechanism immediately and investigate.

* Validate the fail-fast controls locally, demonstrating that no subsequent write occurs after a mismatch.

* Present the results before resuming general REST Issue-body edits.

Keep #1548 open as a reusable write-path testing Issue rather than closing it.

Also proceed with independent review of PR #1566. The amendment must preserve strict integrity verification without unnecessarily interrupting unrelated GitHub operations.

No change to the A1 retirement gates. Continue the r6 independent review and claims-checker design within their existing scope."

As recorded: #1548 stays open. Its current body (SHA-256 `f1e9c22f684b575864bec5004a3776095c5b143b68078cc76a37c2b1602e1062`, 556 bytes) and its comments are preserved on branch `evidence/write-failure-20261125` before the write. That body contains a repository link longer than 101 characters without a fragment, which sec. A.49 rule 1 does not allow to be sent, so the validation body replaces it and cites the preserved copy. REST Issue-body edits otherwise stay suspended until the owner has seen the result.
